summary: Silodosin is a highly selective alpha-1A adrenergic receptor antagonist indicated for the signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH); it is not an antihypertensive. The usual dose is 8 mg once daily with a meal, reduced to 4 mg daily in moderate renal impairment and contraindicated in severe renal (CrCl <30 mL/min) or severe hepatic (Child-Pugh >=10) impairment and with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Key safety concerns are orthostatic/postural hypotension with potential syncope, intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) during cataract surgery, and the need to exclude prostate carcinoma before starting. Retrograde ejaculation is the most common adverse effect.

moa: Silodosin is a selective antagonist of post-synaptic alpha-1 adrenoreceptors located in the prostate, bladder base, bladder neck, prostatic capsule, and prostatic urethra. Blockade of these receptors relaxes smooth muscle in these tissues, improving urine flow and reducing BPH symptoms. It binds with high affinity to the alpha-1A subtype, conferring uroselectivity.

preg: Silodosin is not indicated for use in females.
lact: Silodosin is not indicated for use in females.
renal: Plasma concentrations (AUC and Cmax) are roughly 3 times higher and half-life roughly doubled in moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-50 mL/min) - reduce dose to 4 mg once daily and monitor for adverse events. Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min); not studied in that population. No adjustment needed in mild impairment (CrCl 50-80 mL/min).
hepatic: No dosage adjustment needed in mild or moderate hepatic impairment (single-dose PK not significantly altered in Child-Pugh 7-9). Not studied in and contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score >=10).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - 3.2-3.8x increase in exposure; contraindicated
Strong P-gp inhibitors (e.g., cyclosporine) - increased silodosin concentration; not recommended
Other alpha-blockers - interactions expected; do not use in combination
moderate: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (diltiazem, erythromycin, verapamil) - may increase silodosin levels; use caution and monitor
PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil) - additive vasodilation; potential symptomatic hypotension
Antihypertensive agents - higher incidence of dizziness and orthostatic hypotension; use caution
UGT2B7 inhibitors (probenecid, valproic acid, fluconazole) - may increase exposure
minor: Digoxin - no significant PK change; no dose adjustment required
Silodosin does not inhibit or induce CYP enzyme systems
interactions.food: Take with a meal; a moderate-fat meal decreases Cmax ~18-43% and AUC ~4-49%, and food improves tolerability.
interactions.alcohol: Use caution; alcohol may potentiate orthostatic hypotension and dizziness.
interactions.diagnostics: No laboratory test interactions observed; up to 52 weeks of treatment had no significant effect on PSA.

missed: Take the missed dose with a meal when remembered, unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it and resume the usual once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Dose-limiting adverse event is postural hypotension. If overdose causes hypotension, support the cardiovascular system - keep the patient supine to restore blood pressure and normalize heart rate; give IV fluids if inadequate, and vasopressors if necessary. Monitor and support renal function. Dialysis is unlikely to help because silodosin is highly (97%) protein bound. Silodosin was tolerated up to 48 mg/day in healthy male subjects.
